CLIPORA / GUIDE

Copy several things. Paste the right one.

You do not need to switch back to the original document for every paste. Collect a few copies, then choose each one from your history.

Reviewed 29 October 2026 · Clipora editorial

On this page

Use the history built into Windows

  1. Enable history with Windows + V.
  2. Copy your first piece of text, then the second and third.
  3. Click the destination field. Press Windows + V and select the item you need.
  4. Repeat in the next field. Plain Ctrl + V still uses the current clipboard item.

This is useful for a few recent items. See Microsoft’s history limits and supported formats.

Find an older item with Clipora

With Clipora running and unpaused, copy a synthetic name, an example link and a short reply. In your destination, press Ctrl + Alt + V. Search for part of the text, then click the result or press Enter.

The picker opens near the destination field where Windows exposes its position, with pointer placement as a fallback. Pins stay above ordinary history. Use Shift + Enter to copy without automatic paste.

Use a paste queue for a repeated sequence

Clipora’s item actions can add clips to a paste queue. Arrange the sequence before filling repeated fields, then use the queue action from the app. Keep the order explicit; a queue does not understand form labels or validate that you selected the right field.

For names, addresses or invoices, check each destination before pasting. Clipboard automation should not silently submit forms.

Try it with a harmless example

Name: Morgan Example

Project: Autumn workspace

Reply: Thanks — I will send the draft tomorrow.

Copy each line separately in Windows, then paste them in a different order into a blank document. In the website playground, select “Find an earlier copy” to try the idea without any clipboard access.

When a paste needs your help

Elevated or protected applications can block simulated input. Copy the selected item and use the destination’s own Paste command if automatic paste fails. Very rapid copies can skip intermediate items; pause briefly and check that the important item appeared before moving on.

File clips store file references, not copies of the files. Moving or deleting the original file can break later use.

How to open clipboard history on Windows
